## About

<!-- Deliberately does NOT open with the name, title, and department: the hero
     immediately above carries all three, and this section used to restate them
     as its first sentence — the first thing a reader hit told them nothing they
     had not just read. The work leads now; the background follows it. -->

I work on operations research, optimization, and machine learning — algorithms
that let complex systems decide for themselves, in settings where the
environment is uncertain and the decision has to be made anyway. Most of the
applications come from inventory, manufacturing, and supply chains.

<!-- Three named directions rather than one dense paragraph, and the same three
     that research.qmd carries: one line each here, a paragraph each there. The
     lab site uses the same summary-then-detail split between its home page
     cards and the research sub-pages. -->

<!-- **Data-driven optimization for supply chains** — multi-echelon inventory control
that learns from data instead of an assumed demand distribution.

**Optimization for robotic manufacturing** — scheduling and control for flexible
automation, where the configuration is itself part of what gets optimized.

**Explainable reinforcement learning** — learned policies whose decisions the
people relying on them can actually interpret. -->

I received my Ph.D. in Engineering from Osaka University in 2021, and was an
Assistant Professor at Okayama University before joining Hosei in April 2025.

<!-- The lab used to be a fourth link here as well as having its own section

## Research Group

<!-- Says whose lab it is, which the previous wording left to inference — it

I lead the [Intelligent Systems Laboratory](https://isl-hosei.github.io/) at
Hosei, where students work on the problems above. Prospective students should
start with the lab's Join Us page.
